parties: Pagani Capital Holding (programme sponsor); Indian investors (investors)
headline: Vidhiśāstras advises Pagani Capital on $35M India-focused residency investment programme
sum: Vidhiśāstras structured a $35 million India- and Middle East-focused residency investment programme for Pagani Capital Holding, designed to channel foreign capital into qualifying Indian projects via a Portugal-based residency investment vehicle. The engagement covered regulatory framework, corporate structuring, cross-border compliance, and investor onboarding across India and the Middle East.
implication: Residency investment programmes blending India-focused project deployment with domicile arbitrage (Portugal-issued residency cards) require integrated advice across Indian FDI/FEMA rules, Portuguese residency law, and cross-border fund governance—a novel structuring combining EB-5-style capital raise with EU mobility benefits.
detail: Pagani Capital Holding sought to establish a structured platform offering Indian investors exposure to qualifying projects (sectors unspecified but noted as long-term economic-development focused) with aggregate deployment capped at $35 million. Vidhiśāstras' remit included advising on India-side legal and regulatory compliance (foreign investment, corporate law, FEMA), cross-border transaction documentation, investor protection mechanisms, risk governance, project-level due diligence, and implementation of compliance and onboarding workflows. The programme structure appears to leverage Portugal's Residency-by-Investment scheme while channelling capital into India-based projects, creating a novel cross-border capital-deployment vehicle.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), s. 4 & Schedule I
framework.note: central | Governs inbound foreign investment and cross-border fund flows; defines Overseas Direct Investment and Overseas Investment rules applicable to capital deployment by India-domiciled entities into foreign projects.

framework.ref: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA), s. 5–6
framework.note: central | KYC and beneficial-ownership verification for investor onboarding; applicable to acceptance of foreign capital and cross-border transaction monitoring.
central | Corporate structure and fund governance if programme is domiciled in India or uses India-registered SPV; applicable to constitution, disclosure, and shareholder protections.

framework.ref: Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 (FCRA), s. 4 & rules
framework.note: amended | If programme accepts contributions for political or non-profit activity in India, FCRA compliance may apply; recent amendments (2020–2021) tightened definition of 'foreign contribution'.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Regulations—Alternative Investment Funds Regulations, 2012 (AIF Regulations), r. 2–3
framework.note: If Pagani Capital registers as an AIF or uses India-based fund structure, SEBI registration and governance norms apply to investor accreditation, offering documents, and reporting.

framework.ref: Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), RBI Master Direction on Remittance of Foreign Currency
framework.note: Individual investors may utilize LRS to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for overseas investment; structuring should account for LRS ceilings and documentation.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, s. 42(1), s. 195 (TDS on foreign remittances)
framework.note: TDS compliance on cross-border payments; treaty provisions (India–Portugal DTA) relevant to tax residency and withholding relief.

framework.ref: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA), s. 3–4 (if applicable)
framework.note: If underlying Indian projects include real estate, RERA registration and compliance by project developer required in respective state.

framework.ref: Portuguese Investment Code & Portuguese Residency Investment Scheme (Authorised Regime)
framework.note: On Portugal side: residency card issuance, minimum investment, project classification, and immigration compliance; fund operator must be licensed/registered in Portugal.

structure.consideration: $35 million aggregate capital to be deployed across identified qualifying projects in India and the Middle East.
conditions: Regulatory clearance / reporting under FEMA (if applicable Schedule I investment) and FCRA (if applicable)
Investor KYC and beneficial-ownership verification under PMLA
Project-level legal due diligence and environmental/regulatory clearance in respective jurisdictions
Compliance with Portuguese Residency Investment Scheme requirements and licensing (Portugal-side operator registration)
Investor accreditation and offering document compliance (if SEBI AIF registration triggered)
Cross-border fund-flow and TDS documentation under India–Portugal DTA
approvals: RBI / FEMA approval (if applicable under Schedule I or residency investment outbound remittance rules)
Portuguese financial regulator / immigration authority (residency scheme licensing and investor approval)
State-level project clearances (environmental, real estate, sectoral regulators as applicable to underlying projects)
PMLA / Financial Intelligence Unit India (FIU-IND) reporting if suspicious transaction thresholds breached
structure.novel: Integration of EU residency-by-investment scheme with India-focused project deployment vehicle: investors receive Portuguese residency cards while capital flows into Indian qualifying projects, combining EB-5-style securitization with mobility arbitrage across two jurisdictions.

triggers.law: FEMA, Schedule I & RBI Master Direction on Overseas Investment
triggers.note: Outbound capital deployment by India-domiciled fund operator or investor remittances require RBI/FEMA reporting and sectoral limits (e.g., real estate, banking).

triggers.law: PMLA, s. 4–6 & PMLA Rules 2005 (KYC & beneficial ownership)
triggers.note: Mandatory investor verification, source-of-funds certification, and cross-border transaction monitoring for compliance.

If any programme funds are earmarked for charitable, political, or social activity in India, FCRA registration and prior approval required; amended 2020 rule applies stricter definition of 'foreign contribution'.

If programme is structured as collective fund scheme marketed to Indian residents, SEBI registration as Alternative Investment Fund Category I, II, or III may be mandatory; imposes disclosure, governance, and investor-protection obligations.

triggers.law: Portuguese Decree-Law 89/2017 & Immigration & Tourism Regulatory Authority (Autoridade para a Imigração e Fronteiras) rules
triggers.note: Residency card issuance, fund custody, project classification, and annual compliance reporting with Portuguese regulator required.
